title: RBAC v2: resolve permission-denied and over-permissioned access edge cases during SSO/SCIM provisioning
creator: Ava Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers escalated inconsistent authorization behavior after RBAC v2 rollout. Two classes of faults observed: (1) users receiving 'permission denied' on routes they previously had access to after SAML SCIM syncs or role edits, and (2) intermittent over-permissioning where scoped admin permissions are implicitly granting broader org-level rights. Incidents tied to a combination of RBAC decision cache TTL, SCIM bulk role mapping race conditions, and an edge case in the admin role inheritance rules. Audit logs are incomplete for some of these transitions, complicating root-cause analysis for customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create org with mixed SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning enabled.

2) Create two roles: 'team-admin' (scoped to team) and 'readonly-org' (org-level read). Assign a user via SCIM to 'team-admin' then immediately update user's role via SAML assertion in the same session.
3) Perform API calls to /v1/admin/routes and /v1/instances within 30s of provisioning event; observe authorization responses and audit entries.
4) Repeat with large SCIM bulk import (500+ users) while changing role inheritance in Console to trigger autosync and observe permission flip-flop.
5) Observe logs for RBAC decision cache eviction, and search audit logs for 'role_assignment' events — some events are missing for affected users.
investigation_log: 2026-03-03 - Initial triage: confirmed two customer tickets CS-8812 and CS-8830 showing both permission denied and over-permission scenarios. Reproduced locally with SCIM+SAML repro harness.

2026-03-04 - Found race in SCIM handler: role assignments are written to primary DB but RBAC cache invalidation happens asynchronously; under load invalidation order can be reversed leading to stale decisions.

2026-03-05 - Discovered inheritance bug: when a scoped role is marked 'admin-esque' the computed effective permissions were merging org-level grants due to an earlier optimization in permission union logic (PR ENG-4700).
2026-03-07 - Audit logs: some provisioning transitions (bulk SCIM updates) were being coalesced by the eventing pipeline; downstream audit writer dropped events when backpressure occurred.
2026-03-09 - Customer call with AcmeCorp: provided reproducer and scoped timeline. Customer requested fix + audit rehydration of missing events for compliance (SOC2).
2026-03-11 - Hotfix branch created: fixes for deterministic cache invalidation ordering + strict inheritance check. Added fallback check to refuse granting org-scoped perms from scoped roles.
2026-03-13 - Integration tests updated and added end-to-end SCIM+SAML race tests in CI. QA smoke tests green on staging.
2026-03-14 - Preparing rollout plan for staged deploy; pending security review and sign-off from infra and compliance owners.
proposed_fixes: A. Deterministic cache invalidation: change invalidation to synchronous write-through on role assignment endpoints (SCIM/SAML proxies) for high-risk orgs; keep async invalidation for low-risk paths.
B. Permission union strictness: revert the permissive union optimization and enforce explicit inheritance boundaries so scoped admin roles cannot implicitly escalate to org grants.

C. Audit pipeline resilience: increase the audit writer QPS and add backpressure buffering + guaranteed-at-least-once semantics for role_assignment events. Implement rehydration job to reconstruct missing events from primary DB transaction log for affected time window.
D. Add feature-flag 'rbac_v2_strict_mode' to gate stricter behavior for a canary group of customers before global rollout.
E. Update Console UI to expose 'effective permissions' diffs and last-modified timestamps for roles to aid debugging by SRE/Support.
F. SCIM bulk handler: introduce batch-commit markers and emit explicit 'bulk_sync_start'/'bulk_sync_end' audit events so we can correlate missing events.
G. Add guardrail to SSO session handling: if a SAML assertion changes roles mid-session, force a session refresh to pick up deterministic permissions.
acceptance_criteria: All unit and e2e tests covering SCIM+SAML repros pass in CI.
Staging rollout for 5 canary orgs shows zero regressions for 72h (no perms flip or missing audits).
Audit rehydration job successfully reconstructs missing events for a 24h window in a dry run without data inconsistencies.
Support toolkit updated with a runbook to surface 'last effective policy change' and to manually trigger cache invalidation for customer-facing debug sessions.
Security review complete and compliance owners sign off on audit guarantees.
Post-deploy monitoring alerts in place: sudden increases in 'permission_denied' errors or audit-write-errors trigger an on-call page.
Customer-facing RCA and mitigation plan drafted for affected customers with timeline for rehydration and remediation steps.
qa_plan: Add deterministic CI e2e test that performs SCIM bulk import + immediate SAML role assertion switch under scaled load (500 users).
Simulate eventing pipeline backpressure and ensure audit writer buffers and replays events.
Run fuzz tests on role inheritance combinations to assert no implicit org-wide grants are produced.
Manual verification steps with a staging org: create role changes, execute privileged and non-privileged API calls, confirm audit entries contain role assignment events and timestamps.
Coordinate with Support to run customer repro scenario in a customer-specific sandbox and confirm behavior matches expectations.
Performance check: synchronous invalidation path must not increase median RBAC decision latency beyond 10ms for single-user flows under canary load.
rollback_plan: If a regression is detected during rollout (elevated permission_denied or over-permission events > baseline for 30m), flip feature flag rbac_v2_strict_mode off and revert to previous permission-union code path via the platform rollback pipeline. For audit pipeline regressions, disable new buffering behavior and switch to read-only dry-run mode of the rehydration job.
monitoring: Increase sampling of RBAC decision traces for canary orgs (link to tracing dashboard).
Create metric: 'rbac.permission_denied_rate_by_org' with alert threshold +2x baseline.
Create metric: 'audit.write_error_rate' and 'audit.event_missing_rate' (derived) with immediate P0 alert to on-call.
Add dashboard panels for SCIM bulk sync throughput, event queue length, and cache invalidation latency.
On-call runbook: step-by-step instructions to triage org-specific permissions issues and run rehydration for a given org id.

notes: This ticket contains both immediate customer remediation work and a broader design change to RBAC v2 semantics; split sub-issues created for UI/Console changes and for audit rehydration (ENG-4822, ENG-4823).
Long-term: consider making permission evaluation idempotent across concurrent provisioning flows and exposing a write-ack API contract for SCIM to allow guaranteed consistency windows.
Keep scoped rollouts and runbooks up-to-date; customers under compliance contracts should be offered timely rehydration and signed attestations.
